title: An Investor Letter From Cathie Wood
gist: ARK's Cathie Wood argues the US economy is entering an Industrial-Revolution-scale, technology-driven boom in which inflation collapses even as real GDP growth and short-term interest rates rise together and the yield curve inverts without a recession, favoring equities and bitcoin over fixed income, while oil and gold prices fall and highly-levered 'old economy' private credit faces bankruptcy risk.

themes.theme: Macro regime: back to the Industrial Revolution

insights.claim: Unlike the 1981-2021 disinflationary era, interest rates are now hitting multi-decade 'higher highs' even as US equities climb to record highs, a divergence ARK attributes to a technology-driven productivity boom rather than to inflation.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Investors treating rising rates as a standard equity headwind may be misreading the regime; ARK frames higher rates as a growth signal, not a risk-off signal.
insights.quote: Not since the Industrial Revolution have we witnessed this confluence of economic indicators.

insights.claim: ARK models the current period as structurally analogous to the pre-Great-Depression Industrial Revolution (roughly 3-6% long rates, frequent yield-curve inversions, high real growth) rather than to the post-Depression, low-rate modern era, implying today's higher-rate regime is durable rather than a temporary shock to be reversed.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: If correct, investors modeling a return to 2010s-style near-zero rates are using the wrong historical template; portfolio duration and rate-hedging assumptions should reference the 1800s regime instead.
insights.locator: Interest Rates In The Context Of 200+ Years Of History

themes.theme: Inflation is breaking down faster than official data shows

insights.claim: ARK expects inflation to surprise meaningfully to the downside once war-related oil price spikes subside, driven by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Volcker-style monetary discipline, falling oil prices, and technology-driven deflation.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: A downside inflation surprise would support ARK's case for lower long rates and looser Fed policy sooner than consensus expects, favoring risk assets over cash/short duration.

insights.claim: Warsh has commissioned five Fed task forces, three of which focus on inflation measures, inflation frameworks, and productivity's impact on inflation, and appears open to monitoring real-time private inflation gauges that diverge from official data -- signaling a deliberate Volcker-era-style disinflation campaign.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Watch which inflation gauge (official PCE vs. real-time private data) the Fed leans on -- it will determine how fast rate cuts can be justified.

insights.claim: Real-time Truflation data (tracking 16M+ goods/services daily) shows headline and core PCE inflation already down to 2.5% and 2.1% as of September 2026 -- within 50bps and 10bps of the Fed's 2% target -- versus official BEA headline/core PCE still elevated at 3.7% and 3.3%, implying government inflation statistics are overstating price pressure.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: If real-time data is closer to target than lagging official data, the Fed could ease policy sooner than markets pricing off BEA releases expect -- a potential catalyst for a bond/rate repricing.

themes.theme: Dollar strength and a falling gold price

insights.claim: Contrary to the prevailing 'weak dollar' narrative, the DXY has appreciated more than 35% since the 2008 Global Financial Crisis and the Fed's Broad Dollar Index is 44% above its long-term average, meaning the dollar has actually been strong, not weak, against trading partners.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Investors positioned for continued dollar debasement based on headline narratives may be wrong-footed; ARK expects further dollar appreciation over the next few years akin to the early 1980s.

insights.claim: ARK expects the gold price to decline over the next two years as tax cuts, deregulation, and the technology revolution lift US productivity and returns on invested capital, echoing the more-than-50% gold price drop (from ~$850 to ~$300/oz) during Paul Volcker's Fed tenure.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: A contrarian call against a gold price that just hit an all-time intraday high of $5,595/oz (Jan 29, 2026) -- positions long gold on a 'debasement trade' thesis face valuation risk if ARK's Volcker-analogy plays out.

themes.theme: Oil prices poised for a sharp decline

insights.claim: ARK expects oil prices to fall back to roughly $30-35/barrel over the next few years (from $90-100 currently) once the Strait of Hormuz reopens and OPEC quota discipline breaks down further, drawing a direct parallel to Saudi Arabia's 1986 price war that cut prices ~60% (inflation-adjusted, ~$87 to ~$35/barrel).
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: A sharp oil price decline would act like a broad consumer/business tax cut and reinforce ARK's disinflation thesis; energy-sector and inflation-linked positions should account for this downside scenario rather than assume war-driven prices persist.

insights.claim: OPEC cohesion is fraying: the UAE exited OPEC in May 2026 and raised production 78% (from ~2.3mbd in March to a record ~4.1mbd in June), while Iraq, Nigeria, and Kazakhstan are cheating on quotas and Venezuela is threatening to exit -- leaving Saudi Arabia, which holds ~3.9mbd of spare capacity, as the key swing-producer decision to watch.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Whether Saudi Arabia defends price by cutting output or protects market share by flooding the market (as in 1986) is the pivotal near-term variable for oil price direction.

insights.claim: Because transportation accounts for ~57% of global oil demand and is increasingly transitioning to the electric grid via robotaxis, autonomous trucks, drones, and flying taxis, ARK believes the value of oil reserves may have already peaked secularly at the 2008 price high of ~$145/barrel, incentivizing producers like the UAE to maximize output now rather than hold reserves.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Long-dated oil reserve valuations and producer capex decisions should discount a structurally shrinking demand runway, not assume historical trading ranges persist indefinitely.

themes.theme: Technology-driven deflation is now large enough to move GDP

insights.claim: Five innovation platforms germinating for 20-25 years -- AI, robotics, energy storage, blockchain, and multiomics sequencing -- are now mature enough to meaningfully affect economic growth and inflation, with AI inference costs falling 99%+ per year and whole-genome sequencing costs collapsing from $2.7 billion (2003) to under $100 today.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: This cost-deflation curve is the mechanistic link ARK uses to argue inflation can fall even as growth accelerates -- a key input for positioning across both growth-tech and defensive/inflation-hedge allocations.

insights.claim: Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate rose more than seven-fold from $9 billion in December to $65 billion by July 2026 and could top $100 billion by year-end with rising profitability -- ARK notes this is more revenue growth in seven months than Salesforce achieved in 25 years, offered as evidence against an 'AI hype/bubble' narrative.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Concrete revenue-growth evidence investors can benchmark against 'AI bubble' skepticism when assessing frontier-model company valuations and private AI infrastructure exposure.
insights.quote: Anthropic increased its revenue over seven months by more than Salesforce did in 25 years. No AI "hype" in those numbers!

insights.claim: In 2025, AI inference costs dropped more than 99% while demand for AI inference tokens rose roughly 25-fold, an elasticity combination (falling unit price, exploding volume) that ARK says is now large enough to move macroeconomic growth and inflation statistics.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: This volume/price dynamic is the core mechanism behind ARK's above-consensus GDP growth and below-consensus inflation forecasts -- a lens for stress-testing macro forecasts against AI adoption data.

insights.claim: ARK forecasts real GDP growth could accelerate to 7%+ over the next five years, more than double the ~3% average in place since the Industrial Revolution (and versus 0.6%/year from 1500-1900), because today's five simultaneous innovation platforms outnumber the three that drove the Industrial Revolution (electricity, telephone, internal combustion engine).
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: A sustained 7%+ real growth path, if realized, would be a generational re-rating catalyst for equities broadly and would justify ARK's call to overweight stocks versus bonds.
insights.locator: Real GDP Growth, Productivity, And Interest Rates

insights.claim: Elon Musk is cited as forecasting that AI could increase global GDP growth by 20-30%, an even more aggressive outside estimate than ARK's own 7% base case.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Used by ARK as directional corroboration from a prominent industry figure, though it is a much more extreme number than ARK's own forecast and should be treated as a ceiling scenario, not a base case.
insights.quote: Elon Musk, the inventor of our time, would not be surprised to see real GDP grow 20 to 30% in our time!
insights.locator: Real GDP Growth, Productivity, And Interest Rates

insights.claim: ARK expects sustainable productivity growth to reach 5-6% (versus a ~3.5% peak in the 1980s-90s), giving management teams room to raise margins, boost R&D/capex, raise pay, or cut prices -- and predicts US firms may lean toward price cuts to compete with China while Chinese firms raise wages to rebalance toward domestic consumption, a potential 'win-win' de-escalation of US-China competitive tension.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Watch corporate capital-allocation choices (pricing vs. wages vs. capex) as a signal of how the US-China rebalancing plays out and which margins/sectors benefit.
insights.locator: Real GDP Growth, Productivity, And Interest Rates

insights.claim: ARK expects the yield curve to invert again into negative territory without signaling recession, similar to the pre-1929 Industrial Revolution period when it was inverted more than 60% of the time by roughly 100bps on average, because the inversion would reflect deflationary technology dynamics (short rates tracking nominal growth, long rates discounting falling inflation) rather than a tightening-induced recession.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: If the standard 'inverted curve = recession' signal is broken by this cycle's structure, investors using it as a de-risking trigger could miss the equity upside ARK expects; the curve's shape may need reinterpretation.

insights.claim: ARK forecasts short-term rates could rise to 6-8% in tandem with nominal GDP growth while long rates settle at 5-6%, a rate path that diverges sharply from consensus expectations of Fed rate cuts.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: A scenario where short rates rise rather than fall would punish rate-cut-dependent trades and floating-rate borrowers, while rewarding equities tied to real growth over duration-sensitive fixed income.
insights.locator: Real GDP Growth, Productivity, And Interest Rates

insights.claim: The only precedent since 1929 for a yield-curve inversion without a subsequent recession was the 1966 credit crunch, and the 2022-2024 inversion also did not produce a recession -- evidence ARK uses to argue the historical recession-signal relationship is weakening in this cycle.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Provides a specific historical base rate (1 precedent in ~95 years plus the recent 2022-24 episode) for investors evaluating whether to trust the inverted-curve recession signal this cycle.

insights.claim: Roughly $16 trillion in private equity and private credit, funded primarily with floating-rate debt, is exposed to rising short rates and could face disruption from this technology-driven shift, with the recent SaaS sell-off ('SaaSpocalypse') potentially just the first phase of a broader shakeout among highly levered, technologically disrupted companies.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Investors in private credit/PE vehicles should stress-test portfolio companies for floating-rate exposure and technological obsolescence risk -- a potential source of credit-driven volatility even in a bullish equity scenario.
insights.quote: SaaS-pocalypse may have been just the beginning.
insights.locator: Spoilers: Bankruptcies Amid Unsustainable Government Debt?

insights.claim: A 200-basis-point rise in short rates would add roughly $800 billion to US federal government debt service (nearly the size of the US defense budget) and roughly $300 billion in additional burden across private equity and credit funds, concentrating risk in companies 'on the wrong side of change.'
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Quantifies the fiscal and credit-market stress ARK's own higher-short-rate forecast would create -- a risk to monitor even for investors who agree with the bullish growth thesis.
insights.locator: Spoilers: Bankruptcies Amid Unsustainable Government Debt?

insights.claim: ARK argues debt-to-equity, not debt-to-GDP, is the more relevant solvency metric for economies in growth/productivity mode; despite US Federal Debt-to-GDP being near an all-time high (~125%), Federal Debt-to-US-equity-market-value is near an all-time low, supporting a more constructive read on fiscal sustainability.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: Offers a counter-framework to bearish 'unsustainable debt' narratives -- investors citing debt/GDP as a systemic risk should weigh ARK's debt/equity alternative, which paints a far less alarming picture.
insights.locator: Spoilers: Bankruptcies Amid Unsustainable Government Debt?

insights.claim: ARK's bottom-line asset-allocation call is that the classic 60% equities/40% fixed-income 'balanced portfolio' formula that worked from 1981-2021 should shift toward a higher equity weighting and an allocation to bitcoin, at the expense of fixed income, given ARK's forecast of higher growth, lower inflation, and higher-but-inverted rates.
insights.speaker: ARK Invest Research
insights.so_what: This is ARK's single most directly actionable takeaway: reduce fixed-income duration exposure and add equity and bitcoin weighting to align with the firm's growth/inflation/rate outlook.
insights.quote: In our view, bottom line, get on the right side of change and ride this innovation super cycle!
